module.title: Authentication And Security Fundamentals
module.description: Learn how applications identify users, protect accounts, secure data, and manage authentication systems.

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Authentication is the process of verifying who a user is before allowing access to an application.

sections.heading: Why Authentication Exists
sections.content: Applications need to identify users so private data and accounts stay protected.

sections.heading: How Login Systems Work
sections.content: Users enter credentials like email and password, and backend systems verify them.

sections.heading: Modern Applications Depend On Authentication
sections.content: Social media, banking apps, ecommerce platforms, and dashboards all require authentication.

sections.heading: Authentication vs Authorization
sections.content: Authentication checks who you are, while authorization checks what you are allowed to access.

easyExample.title: School ID Card Example
easyExample.content: A school checks your ID card before allowing entry. Authentication works similarly inside applications.

basicCode.title: Simple Login Check

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Signup creates user accounts while login verifies existing users.

sections.heading: Signup Process
sections.content: Users create accounts by submitting information like username, email, and password.

sections.heading: Backend Validation
sections.content: Backend systems validate user data before creating accounts.

sections.heading: Login Process
sections.content: Users provide credentials which backend systems verify against stored data.

sections.heading: Session Creation
sections.content: After successful login, applications remember the authenticated user.

easyExample.title: Gym Membership Example
easyExample.content: Signup is like creating a gym membership, while login is showing your membership card every visit.

basicCode.title: Signup API Example

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Password hashing converts passwords into secure unreadable values before storing them.

sections.heading: Why Plain Passwords Are Dangerous
sections.content: If passwords are stored directly, hackers could steal and read them easily.

sections.heading: What Hashing Does
sections.content: Hashing transforms passwords into encrypted-looking values that cannot easily be reversed.

sections.heading: Backend Security
sections.content: Modern applications never store real passwords directly in databases.

sections.heading: Password Comparison
sections.content: During login, entered passwords are hashed again and compared securely.

easyExample.title: Secret Code Example
easyExample.content: Instead of storing your real locker password publicly, you store a secret encoded version.

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: JWT (JSON Web Token) allows applications to verify authenticated users securely.

sections.heading: Why JWT Exists
sections.content: Applications need a secure way to remember logged-in users without asking for passwords repeatedly.

sections.heading: What Happens After Login
sections.content: After successful authentication, backend generates a JWT token and sends it to the frontend.

sections.heading: Frontend Stores Token
sections.content: Frontend stores the token and sends it with future requests.

sections.heading: Backend Verifies Token
sections.content: Backend checks the token to confirm the user's identity.

easyExample.title: Movie Ticket Example
easyExample.content: After buying a movie ticket, security checks your ticket instead of asking you to pay again. JWT works similarly.

basicCode.title: JWT Example
basicCode.code: const token = jwt.sign({ id: user.id }, SECRET_KEY);

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Protected routes prevent unauthorized users from accessing private application areas.

sections.heading: Why Route Protection Matters
sections.content: Applications must prevent unauthorized access to sensitive data and features.

sections.heading: What Middleware Does
sections.content: Middleware runs before requests complete and checks user authentication.

sections.heading: Backend Security Flow
sections.content: Protected routes verify JWT tokens before allowing access.

sections.heading: Real Application Usage
sections.content: Dashboards, profile settings, admin panels, and payment systems use protected routes.

easyExample.title: Security Guard Example
easyExample.content: A security guard checks your pass before allowing entry into restricted areas.

lessons.title: Basic Web Security Thinking

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Web security protects applications, users, and data from attacks and unauthorized access.

sections.heading: Why Security Matters
sections.content: Applications store sensitive user information like passwords, payments, and private data.

sections.heading: Frontend Alone Is Not Safe
sections.content: Backend systems must validate and secure all important operations.

sections.heading: Common Security Risks
sections.content: Weak passwords, exposed APIs, and missing authentication create vulnerabilities.

sections.heading: Security Is Continuous
sections.content: Modern applications constantly improve security to prevent attacks.

easyExample.title: Bank Security Example
easyExample.content: Banks use locks, guards, and cameras together for protection. Applications also require multiple security layers.

summary: Modern systems depend heavily on security
